summary: Slow initial response (high TTFB) for streaming requests due to queued quota enforcement amplified by uncoordinated SDK retries
description:
Issue summary:
ClearHealth reports intermittent very slow first-byte (TTFB) on streaming generate calls. Requests eventually return successfully but initial bytes are delayed for up to 10–30s. Customer perceives streaming as hung and has implemented aggressive client retries which coincide with delayed responses.

Impact:
- Multiple production customers at ClearHealth seeing degraded UX for chat streams during peak bursts.
- Apparent service timeouts and duplicate messages due to client retries.
- Business impact: chat flows fail to start or show long pauses, affecting patient-facing triage flows.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod) -> us-east region.
- Customer using Dedicated capacity with reserved pools attached to the account.
- Affected model: redwood-open-13b-v1 pinned.

Steps to reproduce (customer repro):
1) Open a streaming generate with a 2k token system + user prompt payload.
2) Send 20 concurrent streams from multiple pods in their app for bursty traffic.
3) Observe that several streams return first byte after 10–30s while downstream tokens stream normally once started.
4) If SDK is configured with aggressive retry (max backoff 200ms, exponential), additional duplicate requests are seen.

Observed behavior / hypothesis:
- TTFB delays correlate with short-term quota enforcement windows that queue token work on the rate-limiter. A recent change to the rate-limiter added small token-bucketing to improve predictability under high concurrency; this appears to introduce queueing delays at the head of a burst window.
- Customers' SDK retry cadence (small initial backoff + high concurrency) amplifies the queue: duplicates pile up and the queued window takes longer to drain, stretching TTFB for some streams.
- Once a request is dequeued and starts producing tokens, the remainder of the stream proceeds normally (no model regression).

Logs/traces attached by customer:
- Sample request IDs: req_us_776b2a, req_us_776b2b, req_us_776b2c.
- Gateway logs show 429 soft-enforcement events followed by successful handoffs 10–25s later.
- SDK logs show retries fired at 200ms, 400ms, 800ms (customer default), with duplicate X-Request-IDs preserved.

Customer notes:
- ClearHealth observes this behavior multiple times per hour during peak windows (~18:00-19:30 UTC).
- They have temporarily increased client-side initial backoff to 1s which reduced duplicates and symptoms.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 (Support - Aisha Patel): Opened ticket after receiving reproduction logs from ClearHealth. Added initial tracing and requested full gateway log dump for sample request IDs.

2026-03-10 10:07 (Customer - ClearHealth - Dan Liu): We see the UI freeze for 10-30s. Lowering retry aggressiveness helps but doesn't eliminate long TTFB. Happy to run trace with any instrumentation you need.

2026-03-10 13:45 (SRE - Diego Morales): Initial hypothesis: new token-bucketing in rate-limiter may be creating head-of-line queuing during burst windows. Requested infra traces around rate-limiter queue depth and window fill metrics.

2026-03-11 08:32 (SRE - Diego Morales): Correlated gateway logs and rate-limiter metrics. Found periodic small queue spikes aligning with customer bursts. Not a model slowdown; queueing at the rate-limiter looks likely. Prioritizing mitigation and a short-term config change for dedicated pool behavior.

2026-03-12 16:50 (Support - Aisha Patel): Sent workaround instructions to customer: increase client initial backoff to 500-1000ms and enable jitter. Also rolled a dedicated pool config to reduce queueing for pinned dedicated instances. Customer confirms partial improvement.
2026-03-12 17:05 (Customer - Dan Liu): After changes we still see a couple of stalled starts per hour but frequency dropped ~70%. Thanks for the quick mitigation.

2026-03-12 17:40 (SRE - Diego Morales): Engineering follow-up: preparing PR to adjust token-bucket parameters and add instrumentation to surface queueing durations to Console. Will link PRs when available.
2026-03-12 18:05 (Support - Aisha Patel): Marking as In Progress. Working with eng to schedule rollout for low-risk token-bucket tuning and Console metric exposure.
investigation_notes: Attached rate-limiter telemetry for 2026-03-10 18:00-19:30 shows repeated small windows where queued_request_count spikes to 40-80 requests for 8-22s.
Gateway logs for sample req_us_776b2a show 429 soft-enforcement at t=0, no 5xx, then successful admission at t=18s with normal token streaming after that point.
Client-side retry storm confirmed: duplicates carry same session ID leading to multiple queued tokens consuming the same bucket allowance and extending the window.
No anomalous GPU scheduling delays observed on serving-runtime; model token times consistent with baseline.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation (rolled 2026-03-12): adjusted dedicated-pool rate-limiter token-bucket refill to smoother micro-refills to reduce long tail queuing under bursts. Pushed config only to ClearHealth's dedicated pool to minimize blast radius.
Customer recommended client changes: increase initial retry backoff to 500-1000ms and enable randomized jitter. Documented in response and suggested SDK defaults be updated in a follow-up.

Medium-term plan: engineering PR to add a queueing-duration metric to Console, expose per-route queued_request_count, and tune global token-bucket defaults. PRs: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/458 (rate-limiter tuning), https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/212 (queue metrics).
Follow-ups: schedule a postmortem if residual incidents continue after full rollouts; recommend customer test with new SDK backoff defaults once SDK change is released.
